Subject: MSA / Order Form — evidence sprint calendar, pen-test windows, and audit ops checklist

Hi Sara — thanks for the call today. Looping in Laura (legal) and Vanessa (CS) to confirm next steps so procurement has everything to finalize the order form.

Quick recap and asks:
- Neomed asked for SOC 2 Type II report, pen-test access language, and a recurring evidence cadence for quarterly checks.
- Attached: a draft evidence matrix and a proposed pen-test windowing doc (stubs below).

Can you confirm:
1) Whether your security team expects a bounded inspection (timeboxed privileged inspection) or full ongoing inspection rights in the MSA?
2) Prefered pen-test window(s) — we proposed two 5-business-day windows (see attachment) but can adjust.
3) Any special procurement requirements for logs/retention beyond our standard 90 days?

Proposed next steps: I'll circulate a short operations checklist for the evidence cadence and a suggested clause for the security exhibit that narrows the scope to SOC 2 controls and agreed pen-test windows. If that looks good we can push the redline to your legal via the DocuSign orderform link next week.

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@neomedhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — evidence sprint calendar, pen-test windows, and audit ops checklist

Thanks Aditya — that recap is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from Neomed Security: 

- We prefer a bounded inspection model (timeboxed privileged inspection) tied to a notice window and limited to specific control groups. Our usual verbiage includes a maximum of two inspection periods per year, each 5 business days, with scope limited to SOC 2 in-scope systems.
- For pen tests we need a single 30-day blackout notice before the scheduled window (procurement wants calendar certainty). If Redwood can commit to two available windows in the next 90 days, procurement should be able to align.
- Retention: we require event logs to be retained 180 days for the systems in-scope for SOC2. Is that compatible with your standard?

I'll have procurement (procureops@neomedhealth.com) confirm official dates once we lock language. Laura/Vanessa — happy to take any redline suggestions.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Director, Security Operations
Neomed Health

Laura / Vanessa — forwarding Sara's reply. Key asks: bounded inspection (max two 5-business-day windows/yr), 30-day blackout notice for pen tests, 180-day log retention for SOC2 in-scope systems.

Can legal draft a narrow security exhibit that: 
- Limits inspection rights to SOC 2 in-scope systems and requires notice + mutually agreed schedule;
- Limits number/length of inspections (we prefer language like "up to two timeboxed inspections per rolling 12-month period, each no more than five business days");
- Adds a requirement that Redwood's standard retention meets 180 days for in-scope logs (or we propose an order-form appendix for this);
- Includes pen-test coordination language that requires disclosure of test window and scope, with an agreed blackout window for maintenance.

Vanessa — customer expects calendar availability in the next 90 days. Can we commit to two windows? If operations can propose dates, we'll include them in the order form.

I attached a draft evidence matrix and a short redline summary I can share with Sara if legal signs off.

Thanks — Aditya

Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA / Order Form — evidence sprint calendar, pen-test windows, and audit ops checklist

Thanks for the context. Draft guidance below so we can get a clean redline out today: 

- Inspection clause: We'll propose "timeboxed inspection" language that requires at least 10 business days' notice for a standard inspection and caps inspections at two per 12-month period, each no longer than five business days. Add scope definition: "inspection limited to SOC 2 in-scope systems and controls as listed in the order form appendix."
- Pen-test language: Require 30 days' advance notice, mutually agreed scope and a requirement that Redwood be notified of any elevated findings within 5 business days. We will avoid language that grants external testers live admin credentials unless explicitly approved for a specified window and supervised by Redwood staff.
- Retention: We can commit to 180 days for event logs on in-scope systems if the customer signs the order-form appendix that lists the specific products/agents in scope (to avoid a broad system-wide commitment).

I'll attach a short redline snippet for legal to drop into the security exhibit. If legal wants stricter verbiage (e.g., log encryption at rest details), we can coordinate with infra but keep the MSA appendix narrow.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Subject: RE: MSA / Order Form — evidence sprint calendar, pen-test windows, and audit ops checklist

Sara / ProcureOps — thanks for confirming the preferences. Per Karthik's guidance we've prepared a narrow security exhibit and an order-form appendix that: 
- Defines inspection as timeboxed, limited to SOC 2 in-scope systems, max two inspections per rolling 12 months, each up to five business days;
- Requires 30 days' notice for pen tests and mutual agreement on scope;
- Commits to 180-day retention for event logs for systems listed in the appendix;
- Prohibits permanent admin credential handoff — any elevated tester access will be supervised and explicitly scoped for the inspection window.

I've attached the redline summary as a PDF and the evidence matrix; if procurement can confirm one preferred 5-day window in September (any week starting Sep 7 or Sep 21) we'll lock calendar slots and push the order form for signatures. DocuSign/orderform link is in related links.

Next actions (simple checklist):
- Neomed (ProcureOps) picks preferred 5-day inspection window by EOD Aug 18
- Redwood legal to drop security exhibit redline into order form (we'll send by Aug 17)
- Procurement to confirm SOC2 Type II acceptance (or request additional attestations)
- Ops to confirm logging scope list (we'll share appendix with product names)

Thanks — looking forward to closing.

Best,
Aditya
